title: Limit of Detection (LOD), Blank-Based Estimate

references.label: General microbiology/quantitative methods references (ASM, FDA BAM)

explanation: A commonly used working estimate for the lowest signal that can be reliably distinguished from background/blank noise, based on repeated measurement of a blank (a sample containing no analyte). Using 3 standard deviations above the blank mean is a widely used convention, though the exact multiplier and the full validation approach depend on the specific assay, regulatory context, and standard being followed — this is a simplified working formula, not a substitute for a full formal LOD determination.

variables.meaning: Average signal measured across repeated blank (analyte-free) samples
Standard deviation of the repeated blank measurements

workedExample.scenario: Repeated blank measurements on a spectrophotometric assay give a mean absorbance of 0.020 with a standard deviation of 0.004.
workedExample.result: LOD ≈ 0.032 absorbance units (converted to a concentration via the assay's standard curve)

commonMistakes: Estimating LOD from too few blank replicates, giving an unstable standard deviation and an unreliable LOD estimate.
Confusing LOD (lowest reliably detectable signal) with LOQ (lowest signal that can be reliably and precisely quantified, which uses a larger multiplier such as 10×SD).
Treating a single-lab blank-based LOD estimate as equivalent to a fully validated, multi-site LOD determination.
